title: Dimension of an algebraic space under a field extension
statement: Let $k\to K$ be a field extension [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $Y$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum], separated and of finite type: its diagonal is a closed immersion and it is quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts (using [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] for the scheme conventions). Then $Y_K=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with the scheme convention [def-pc-fibre-product], has the same topological Krull dimension as $Y$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]: $\dim |Y_K|=\dim |Y|$, where $|Y|$ and $|Y_K|$ carry the atlas topology on point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Empty spaces are included, with dimension $-\infty$.

source.place: Tag 04NS (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), part (1), specialized to a field extension; topological dimension agrees with etale-chart dimension for separated spaces by decent-spaces.tex, Tag 0A4J (lemma-dimension-decent-space) and Tag 088J (lemma-locally-separated-decent). The separated finite-type version is asserted here.

proof.text: The separatedness hypothesis implies that $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-separated. Indeed, after any scheme test the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its inverse image over a quasi-compact open is homeomorphic to a closed subset of that open, which is quasi-compact. Thus the diagonal is quasi-compact on every scheme test, exactly the hypothesis in the atlas dimension comparison used below.

source.place: Tag 088J (lemma-locally-separated-decent); quasi-separatedness verified directly from the closed diagonal

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $a:U\to Y$ with $U$ a scheme [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The chart criterion [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test], with target chart $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ the identity, makes $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ locally of finite type. Put $U_K=U\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$, a scheme [def-pc-fibre-product]. The algebraic-space fibre-product and covering theorem [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] makes $Y_K$ an algebraic space and supplies a surjective etale atlas $U\times_Y Y_K\to Y_K$. This source is $U_K$: a test point of either product is precisely a pair $(u,t)$ with the same image in $\operatorname{Spec}k$, since the $Y$ coordinate is forced to be $a(u)$. The mutually inverse compatible-pair maps respect both projections. Now [lem-sfb-space-etale-atlas-topological-dimension] applied to the quasi-separated $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, first with $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and then with $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$, gives $\dim|Y|=\dim U$ and $\dim|Y_K|=\dim U_K$. No assertion of quasi-compactness of the chosen atlas is needed.

source.place: Tag 04NS (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), atlas reduction in the proof; Tag 040Y (lemma-finite-type-local); decent-spaces.tex Tag 0A4J (lemma-dimension-decent-space)

proof.text: If $U$ is empty then $U_K$ is empty, since its projection has target $U$. Both scheme dimensions are $-\infty$ by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], so Step 2 proves the desired equality. Otherwise apply [lem-pc-dim-base-change-affine-covers] to the locally finite type scheme $U$ and the given field extension. It states that $U_K$ is nonempty and provides matching affine open covers $U_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of $U$ and $V_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_kK)$ of $U_K$, with every $A_i$ finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tag 04NS (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), reduction to scheme charts; schemes.tex Tags 01JR and 01JQ, and morphisms.tex Tag 01T0, for matching affine charts

proof.text: In the nonempty case, the first clause of [lem-pc-dim-base-change] applies to each finite type $k$-algebra $A_i$ and gives $\dim(A_i\otimes_kK)=\dim A_i$ as ring dimensions. Apply [lem-pc-dimension-affine-open-cover] to each of the two nonempty schemes and the covers of Step 3. These formulas use the supremum of stalk ring dimensions; [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] identifies that supremum with topological Krull dimension. Consequently $\dim U_K=\sup_i\dim(A_i\otimes_kK)=\sup_i\dim A_i=\dim U$. Substitute the two atlas equalities of Step 2 to conclude $\dim|Y_K|=\dim|Y|$. The argument compares suprema term by term, so no purity, irreducibility, reducedness, algebraicity or separability assumption on the extension enters.

proof_origin.place: Tag 04NS (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), proof via scheme atlases, with decent-spaces.tex Tags 0A4J and 088J, algebra.tex Tag 00P3, and properties.tex Tag 04MU.
